chunks: Whenever a Surah is revealed (which says): "Believe in God and fight along with His Prophet," the well-to-do among them ask for leave to stay at home, and say: "Leave us with those who are left behind."

key_terms.أُولُوا الطَّوْلِ: The well-to-do / those with wealth and status
key_terms.الْقَاعِدِينَ: The seated / those who stay behind or are idle

ai.seo_question: How did the wealthy hypocrites react when commanded to fight in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Surah At-Tawbah, this verse highlights the 'Ahl al-Dhul' (men of wealth and status) among the hypocrites who, upon the revelation of a command to strive with their wealth and selves, sought exemption to remain with the idle. Shia exegetes often link this reluctance to the broader theme of 'Taqwa' (God-consciousness) versus superficial faith, illustrating how material comfort can hinder spiritual commitment. The verse serves as a critique of those who prioritize worldly ease over the rigorous demands of jihad and sincerity in following the Prophet.
